Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental error in applying geographical and meteorological principles. It incorrectly assumed that a 50 km distance corresponds to a significant latitudinal temperature difference (~0.6-0.7°C) while simultaneously underestimating the impact of elevation. In reality, the environmental lapse rate is approximately 6.5°C per 1,000 meters; therefore, an elevation difference of just 850 meters (which is common within a 50 km radius) would result in a ~5.5°C temperature difference. This is far more substantial than the latitudinal effect over 50 km. The Planner's reasoning was flawed because it relied on a miscalculation of the magnitude of latitudinal gradients versus elevation gradients, leading to the selection of the wrong answer (Latitude) instead of the correct one (Elevation).
